42 files against main. Planned: schema.prisma, the clinical_core migration, memory-prisma.ts, seed.ts, ERD.md, the four test files, spec/plan/tasks/traceability/tasks.json, the implementation and test reports, and the governance verification record. Disclosed and outside the feature's plan: the backoffice port move 5173 to 5174 with its five consumer sites (requested separately by the owner, see F5), the verify.js and product-plan.js framework patches the feature's own verification depends on (F4), and the .prettierignore additions for .prisma and .sql. Branch matches feature.branch and is based on main. One path is uncommitted: .sdrive/audit-log.json - F2.

14 tests; every name carries both its TEST-### id and its AC or NFR id. Zero .only, xit or xdescribe. Three intentional skips, each documented: the two database suites skip with a reason when Docker is absent, and TEST-014 needs no database. Assertions are behavioural - row counts read back from PostgreSQL, index definitions, migration state - not string matching on the implementation.

pnpm --filter server run lint exit 0; pnpm --filter server run typecheck exit 0; prettier --check exit 0 on every changed file once .prisma and .sql are excluded (F4). Both recorded in implementation report section 9.

spec.md section 6 records the security baseline: CON-511 to CON-515, CON-517 and CON-518 are NOT APPLICABLE with reasons (no credentials, route, header, rate limit, DTO, UI or state-changing endpoint is added). The two REQUIRED controls are met - CON-516: the migration is static DDL with no DROP, TRUNCATE or ALTER COLUMN, asserted on comment-stripped SQL by TEST-009; CON-519: the seed reads DATABASE_URL from the environment only and refuses NODE_ENV=production, asserted by TEST-014, and seeded identities use reserved fixture domains (TEST-013). No security report exists for this feature because no auditable surface - auth, input, transport, secrets handling - changes; that is stated here rather than left implicit.

Recorded run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 over four files - 14 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 61 s wall clock. schema.test.mjs 5/5 needs no database; migrations.test.mjs 4/4 and seed.test.mjs 5/5 ran against a real PostgreSQL 16 container the suite starts and owns (port 55432), with a scratch database per file.

server/prisma/ERD.md documents the clinical models, their relations to Clinic and to each other, and both indexes, with schema.prisma named as the source of truth. The implementation report records the migration, seed, guards and the gate results; the test report records method, mapping and NFR numbers. README is untouched because nothing user-facing changed - the schema is internal until BP-015 exposes it, and documenting endpoints that do not exist yet would be false.

All four NFRs are measured or directly asserted. NFR-001 migrate deploy: 8.2 s in the recorded run, 7.4-15.4 s across runs, against a 60 s budget (TEST-007). NFR-003 seed: 16.5 s in the recorded run, 19-30 s across runs, against 60 s (TEST-011); one run under heavy load measured 61.3 s and is disclosed in the report as a breach rather than dropped (F1). NFR-002 additive-only: TEST-009 applies the clinical migration to a populated database and confirms the rows survive. NFR-004 clinic scoping: TEST-001 asserts clinicId is a foreign key, not just a column.

Every DoD item is satisfied or disclosed: constitution and feature files read; all 9 tasks complete; 9 of 9 ACs tested at 100%; traceability complete; evidence bound to HEAD; lint, typecheck and formatting clean; the security baseline recorded in the spec with its two required controls tested; NFR evidence recorded. Disclosed rather than passed: the one NFR-003 breach under load and the absent CI run. Nothing is claimed that was not observed.
sdrive verify database-schema-and-migrations = PASS (matched 41, missing 0, renamed 0, extra 0), well inside CON-602.

gh run list --branch feature/bp-002-bp-003-bp-006-bp-031 returns no runs for this branch or for HEAD 7bb2824. .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on pushes to main/master and on pull requests only, and the review agent may not open a PR. Separate from this feature: the workflow cannot pass yet even on main, because @prisma/client exports nothing on a clean checkout until `pnpm --filter server exec prisma generate` runs after install. Recorded, not passed.

The workspace has a single member (kenule500, admin) who implemented the feature and requested this review. The conflict is recorded, and the PASS was not self-approved: the human confirmed it explicitly at the decision gate.

findings.issue: NFR-003 (the seed completes in under 60 s) was breached once at 61.3 s on a heavily loaded machine; four other runs measured 16.5-30 s. The test report states the breach, the range and the likely cause (ts-node recompiles the script on every invocation), and recommends re-measuring on a CI runner rather than trusting a laptop.

.sdrive/audit-log.json is the only uncommitted path. Every sdrive command appends a hash-chained entry, so the evidence run that C06 requires necessarily dirties the tree - the same tension that made test-evidence.json gitignored.

No CI run exists for this branch. The workflow triggers on main/master pushes and pull requests only, and it would fail even then because the Prisma client is never generated on a clean checkout, so @prisma/client exports nothing and typecheck cannot resolve PrismaClient.

The branch carries three changes the feature's own verification depends on: verify.js now collects .prisma and .sql, reads workspace manifests, matches on-disk paths and compares dependency names case-insensitively; product-plan.js repairs a double-encoded dependency cell that had frozen the product plan's start wave; .prettierignore excludes .prisma and .sql because Prettier has no parser for them. Without the first, sdrive verify reports the schema as missing and C15 cannot pass. All three are hash-pinned or disclosed in CONTRIBUTING.

Commit da46c5a moves the backoffice dev server from 5173 to 5174 along with its five consumer sites and the docs. It is unrelated to BP-002 and was requested separately while this feature was in flight; it should ideally have been its own change rather than riding a database feature's branch.

workflow-state.json registers BP-003, BP-006 and BP-031 against this same branch, each with only a branch-created history entry. Archiving BP-002 merges this branch to main; those features still need their own specs and, at that point, their own branches.
Reviewer and implementer are the same workspace member, so the review is not independent. Recorded under C18 and human-confirmed.
